body: Solstice is Software Creations' isometric puzzle adventure for the NES. The wizard Shadax enters the fortress of Kâstleröck to collect six pieces of the Staff of Demnos and rescue Princess Eleanor from Morbius. Its 250 rooms form a connected space, with each chamber presenting another arrangement of platforms, objects and hazards. Shadax can jump, lift and place objects. Those few actions make an apparently compact room demanding, because reaching a doorway can depend on understanding how several objects occupy the same three-dimensional space.

Four kinds of potion can grant temporary protection, remove moving objects, stop time or reveal invisible objects. Their effects last within the current room, encouraging the player to use a limited supply where it creates a practical opening. A falling block frozen in place can become a step. Other blocks can be moved into routes over dangerous floors. The isometric view makes these arrangements immediately visible, while judging their heights and positions remains part of solving the problem.

A map records visited rooms and their possible exits, helping the player relate individual puzzles to the larger fortress. Keys, hidden passages and useful items make a familiar chamber worth returning to later. Software Creations had previously concentrated on conversions; Solstice was its first original game. Tim Follin's elaborate score gives the opening a striking musical presence before the careful movement begins. The later Super NES sequel, Equinox, continued this interest in spaces whose routes have to be assembled through objects and observation.
